items.title: Ken Peplowski interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 10, 1997 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: He was a very tough band leader though. We could go through a whole rehearsal and not get past the first eight bars of a tune.

ctx.x: He was a tight-lipped guy. He’s not the evil person that you’ve heard in a lot of books or interviews. He was a complex guy. I think he really didn’t know how to deal with his fame. He was uncomfortable about it and I think almost his whole life revolved around music, to the exclusion, unfortunately, of thinking about people’s feelings and things like that. But he just was obsessed with music. He practiced all the time. He was always thinking about those old Fletcher Henderson charts, how can I play them and make…

the way he wanted it and I think he liked that. He was a very tough band leader though. We could go through a whole rehearsal and not get past the first eight bars of a tune. Very tough, very demanding, but he got results. And he whipped us into shape and made us sound like a Benny Goodman band. He was no more tough or crazy than Buddy Rich for example.
What was in his instructions that made you sound like a Benny Goodman band?
